name: scope-fence-negative
description: The public-ingress fence, graded rather than assumed: a decision written by an authenticated client is recalled by a member of its tenant through enumeration, unprompted volunteering and search, while the static public bearer is refused the first two outright and structurally returned nothing by the third — yet can still fetch the page it names.

args.title: Retire the Legacy Importer
args.markdown_body: The Legacy Importer is retired at the end of Q3; everything moves to the streaming ingest path.

args.fact: The Legacy Importer is retired at the end of Q3.

probes.note: Continuity by name: a client that never saw the write resolves the author's alias to the author's slug.

Leak case paired with member-resolve. resolve_slugs enumerates author-written identifiers, so the shipped ingress denylist refuses it for the public bearer BEFORE dispatch — and dispatch alone would hand it over, which is exactly why the fence is graded here rather than assumed.

args.window: user: Is the Legacy Importer still running?

probes.note: The unprompted path inside the tenant.

args.window: user: Is the Legacy Importer still running?

probes.note: Leak case paired with member-volunteer. Same denylist, different surface: slugs, titles and synopses volunteered to an anonymous caller would be the same disclosure resolve_slugs is refused for.
The retrieval arm, over the page mirror the write created. Runs on a deterministic embedder, so the vector arm is exercised without Bedrock.

The one public refusal that is NOT the denylist: search is open to the public bearer, and page-derived hits are dropped from the result instead. A different mechanism from the two above, and it fails differently, so it is worth its own probe.

Not a leak — a positive label, and the capability control for the three refusals above. The public bearer may FETCH a page whose slug it already knows (the body is redacted); what it may not do is enumerate its way to one. If page_get is ever added to the public denylist this pin breaks, and the pin is what should be updated.
